what: Old Dominion Freight Line is a trucking company specialising in less-than-truckload freight, where shipments from many customers share one trailer. It runs its own terminal network and is known for the best service record in the industry.
customers: Manufacturers, retailers and distributors shipping pallets rather than full truckloads across the United States.
money: freight moved through its terminal network
moat: A terminal network built over decades with spare capacity bought ahead of demand, and a damage and on-time record that lets it charge more than competitors.
risks: Freight volumes have fallen for three years in the industry downturn
Its fixed terminal costs do not shrink when volumes do
It trades at a high multiple relative to other trucking companies
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 23% with an operating margin of 25%, both the best in the industry
Almost no debt: about $20 million against $466 million of cash
A freight recovery would flow through to profits quickly given spare terminal capacity
watch: Tonnage per day and revenue per hundredweight.
